title: Arista Lines Up Networking For 10 Gigawatts Of AI Systems
gist: Arista's Q3 2026 revenue rose 58.5% to $3.66B with record 42.7% net margin, as AI front-end and scale-across routing finally produce a hockey-stick ramp; CEO Jayshree Ullal expects AI networking to double from about $3.5B in 2026 to $7B in 2027 and to network 10 gigawatts of AI capacity by end-2027. The author argues Ethernet (ESUN, UALink) will eventually displace Nvidia's proprietary NVLink/NVSwitch, but Arista's scale-up trials only start in 2027 with production in 2028.

insights.claim: The author argues AI networking requires high-radix devices and flatter networks because workloads are latency sensitive and idle GPUs or XPUs are economically devastating given their cost, unlike the 2010-2020 cloud era of riding down cost per bit.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Network performance directly drives AI cluster ROI, supporting premium pricing for AI-optimized switches.
insights.quote: keeping these compute engines waiting is economically devastating

insights.claim: Balancing workloads across hundreds of thousands to millions of accelerators requires AI embedded in network management, such as Arista's Autonomous Virtual Assistant, and AI-driven security because attackers also use AI.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Software and telemetry become differentiators and recurring revenue for network vendors.

insights.claim: The author contends that no one except Nvidia — not hyperscalers, cloud builders, model builders, HPC labs, sovereigns or AMD — wants proprietary AI networks, and that NVSwitch and NVLink will face cheaper Ethernet-based ESUN and UALink alternatives as InfiniBand did.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Long-term threat to Nvidia's networking margins and opportunity for Ethernet switch and UALink ASIC vendors.
insights.quote: NVSwitch and NVLink are the InfiniBand of scale up and scale in networking

insights.claim: Arista currently makes money on cloud and AI front-end networks and on its R series routing switches for scale-across links spanning datacenters and regions, needed because local power limits cap datacenter size, but has no serious scale-up revenue yet.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Power-constrained geography drives multi-site AI clusters and demand for scale-across routing.
insights.locator: But this transition is going to take time.

insights.claim: Jayshree Ullal said Arista has worked with AMD, Arm, Meta Platforms, Microsoft and Qualcomm on rackscale switching, with ESUN scale-up trials starting in 2027 at 128 or 144 accelerators per rack and about 1,000 per row, and production rollouts not expected until 2028.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Ethernet scale-up revenue is a 2028+ story, so Nvidia's NVLink position is safe near term.
insights.locator: On a call with Wall Street analysts

insights.claim: Arista has not committed to UALink switching, which would compete more directly with NVSwitch, though third-party UALink ASICs from Astera Labs, Marvell, Upscale AI and possibly Panmnesia make it possible; on-package scale-in remains the domain of AMD, Nvidia, Broadcom, Marvell, Alchip and possibly Intel and Qualcomm.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Maps which vendors compete at each layer of the AI interconnect hierarchy.
insights.locator: Arista has not said it will embrace UALink

insights.claim: Arista's Q3 2026 product sales rose 66.9% year on year and 22.4% sequentially to $3.19 billion, and total revenue rose 58.5% to $3.66 billion with 20.5% sequential growth, 2x to 3x its normal sequential rate.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Evidence the long-awaited GenAI hockey stick in Arista's revenue has begun.
insights.locator: In the September quarter, Arista posted

insights.claim: Arista's Q3 2026 operating income rose 67.9% to $1.64 billion and net income rose 82.9% to $1.56 billion, a record 42.7% of revenue, with $14.36 billion cash, $11.4 billion purchase commitments and $6.84 billion deferred revenue.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Record profitability plus large deferred revenue and commitments give strong forward visibility.

insights.claim: Ullal said Arista is on track for about $3.5 billion in AI front-end and back-end networking in 2026, doubling to about $7 billion in 2027, with campus switching growing from $1.25 billion to $2 billion.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: AI networking doubling implies continued share gains, including campus share from Cisco.
insights.locator: On the call, Ullal said that Arista

insights.claim: At the midpoint of targets Arista will grow revenue 52% to $13.3 billion in 2026 and 39.1% to $18.5 billion in 2027, while the author notes core cloud switching and edge segments are growing only modestly.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Growth is concentrated in AI and scale-across routing, increasing dependence on AI capex.
insights.locator: At the midpoint of growth targets

insights.claim: Arista's 10%-plus customers Microsoft and Meta Platforms are working with it on ESUN scale-up networks for their Maia and MTIA XPUs, and Ullal said one or two more big spenders may be added in the coming year.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Customer concentration persists but potential new hyperscale customers would diversify 2027 growth.

insights.claim: Ullal said Arista went from four or five customers with 50,000-100,000 Nvidia GPU clusters in 2024-2025, when much InfiniBand was still deployed, to more than 100 Etherlink AI customers in 2026, and forecasts networking 10 gigawatts of AI capacity linking ten or more accelerator types by end-2027.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Rapid broadening of the AI Ethernet customer base signals InfiniBand displacement and accelerator diversity.
